🔥 The fire settles. Hunter has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Tanya says "Say that again — slower." Thabo breathes "And you're still standing." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

fightLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Carmela Hao. Sign painter. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dog tags, Field suture kit, Mixtape, Dispatcher's headset, Seed packet. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morning. Inside out. Not eaten — unmade. Like something was trying to understand how it worked. It didn't finish.
